title: Service protection guardrails coordination plan — Q2 2026
content:
Context:
This is a practical coordination plan for a cross-functional program to put lightweight protection guardrails around service launches and model rollouts. The goal is to reduce regressions in availability/latency during feature/model rollouts, make SLOs actionable for feature teams, and create fast fallbacks when signals degrade. This doc captures proposed sprint work, responsibilities, decision criteria, and an initial communication/runbook surface.

Key objectives (Q2):
- Define 3 pragmatic SLO tiers (critical, standard, experimental) and mapping guidance for product/feature teams.
- Implement a minimal cross-team scaffold: pre-launch checklist, launch-time telemetry dashboard, and rollback playbook.
- Create automation for fast fallback to lower-cost/safer model variant or cached responses on signal thresholds.
- Pilot with 2 product launches (hosting + embeddings path) and iterate.

Scope & out-of-scope:
- In-scope: SLO definitions, launch checklists, alert thresholds, rollback/runbook templates, dashboard templates, basic failover automation for model variant fallback.
- Out-of-scope: Major infra refactors, complete on-call rewrite, long-term cost optimization experiments (deferred to Optimize team).

Roles & owners (initial):
- Program lead: Priya Shah (platform-engineering) — overall coordinator, weekly syncs, exec updates.
- SLO design: Marcus Lee (site-reliability-engineering) — define measurement, error budgets, thresholds.
- Observability & dashboard: Aisha Thompson (observability) — dashboard templates, instrumentation checklist.
- Serving fallback automation: Diego Fernandez (serving-runtime) — implement model-variant fallback hook + feature flag.
- Product pilot owners: Rachel Kim (product-hosted-api) + two feature PMs (TBD).

High-level timeline (8 weeks):
- Week 1 (Mar 16–20): Kickoff, align definitions, pick pilot features. Deliverable: short decision doc with chosen pilot features.
- Week 2 (Mar 23–27): Draft SLO tier definitions + pre-launch checklist. Deliverable: SLO tier doc + checklist draft.
- Week 3 (Mar 30–Apr 3): Implement telemetry spec for dashboards and alerts; instrumentation tasks opened.
- Week 4 (Apr 6–10): Build dashboard templates (latency/availability/kvs/queue depth + token-level breakdown). Create alert runbook stubs.
- Week 5 (Apr 13–17): Implement simple fallback automation (feature-flagged). Run internal smoke tests.
- Week 6 (Apr 20–24): Pilot launch with product A (hosted API feature). Observe for 7 days; capture lessons.
- Week 7 (Apr 27–May 1): Iterate on thresholds, patch runbook, onboard product B (embeddings).
- Week 8 (May 4–8): Retro, finalize lightweight playbook, propose handoff cadence for Q3.

SLO tier definitions (proposal):
- Critical (target availability >= 99.95%, p50 latency < 150ms for small responses) — customer-facing core calls; requires dedicated on-call and runbook. Error budget burn rate > 3x in 1h => immediate rollback/fallback.
- Standard (target availability >= 99.9%, p50 latency < 200ms) — majority of production traffic; oncall via rotation, automated alerting triggers investigation.
- Experimental (target availability >= 99.5%, p50 latency < 350ms) — early-stage features and research models; accept higher variability, automated soft-fail to cached/cheaper model when error budget rapid burn detected.

Pre-launch checklist (to be completed by feature team + infra):
- SLO tier chosen and documented (link to SLO doc).
- Instrumentation: metrics emitted (success/total, p50/p95/p99 latency, token counts, model variant id).
- Dashboards: baseline dashboard created with historical baselining for last 14 days.
- Alerting: alerts created with paging thresholds + non-paging ops channel thresholds.
- Fallback: feature-flagged fallback path implemented and smoke-tested.
- Runbook: owner and escalation path declared; rollback steps validated in staging.

Launch-time telemetry & alerts (starter set):
- Immediate paging alert: availability < target (tier dependent) for rolling 5m window AND error-rate spike > 3x baseline.
- Degradation alert: p95 latency > threshold for 10m window — non-paging to SLT but pages SRE if sustained 30m.
- Token-cost alert: average token consumption > 1.5x baseline for 1h — non-paging.
- Model drift/quality (where applicable): % rerank/regression > threshold — triggers quality review, not immediate rollback (unless tied to availability).

Fallback automation (implementation notes):
- Approach: small controller in serving-runtime that subscribes to alert events or polls metrics. When configured thresholds hit and feature flag enabled, switch traffic to preconfigured fallback plan: (a) pinned model variant (lower-latency/quantized), or (b) deterministic cached response layer for top-K prompts.
- Safety: fallback requires opt-in on a per-route basis; must be gated behind a feature flag and have an operator-exposed kill switch.
- Observability: every fallback action must emit event with reason, snapshot of metrics, and link to active runbook.

Pilot evaluation checklist (post 7-day observation):
- Did SLO hold? (yes/no, with burn rate)
- How did fallback behave (if triggered)? Latency/cost delta.
- False positives/alert noise count.
- Time-to-detect and time-to-recover median.
- Action items and owners for Q3 handoff.

Decision criteria for automatic rollback vs manual intervention:
- Auto-fallback allowed when availability breach AND error-rate spike clear AND pilot feature explicitly opted in.
- Manual rollback required when data-quality/regression metrics exceed tolerance even if availability nominal.

Communications & cadence:
- Weekly cross-functional sync (30 min) — program lead + all owners.
- Daily quick stand (10 min) during pilot launch week for product A.
- Slack channel: #guardrails-program (create thread per pilot deployment).
- Executive checkpoint doc: one-pager after pilot (deliver to Eng VP and Product leads).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Alert fatigue and noisy thresholds => Mitigation: conservative thresholds, non-paging first, short pilot to tune.
- Risk: Fallback causes correctness regressions => Mitigation: require product opt-in, test harness comparing outputs, canary rollouts.
- Risk: Lack of instrumentation on legacy paths => Mitigation: instrument baseline scripts and require minimal metrics before launch.

Open questions / TODOs (owner):
- Decide precise numeric thresholds for p95/p99 per tier (Marcus) — due Week 2.
- Identify pilot feature PMs and engineering leads (Rachel) — due Mar 18.
- Small PoC for fallback controller (Diego) — spike story PLAT-910.
- Confluence SLO template to publish (Priya) — link in linked_artifacts when ready.

Appendix: quick checklist for product PM before sign-off:
- Confirm SLO tier mapping and accept consequences (error budgets).
- Confirm fallback plan and opt-in flag exists.
- Confirm observability has historical baseline and dashboards.
- Confirm runbook owner and communication path.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the first pilot narrow and observable. Don’t over-automate initial rollbacks — prefer human-in-the-loop for first two runs.
- Keep documentation terse with templates that teams can copy.
- Capture case studies from pilot for Q3 playbook expansion.
